analysis.title: Half A Trillion In IOUs, A Dead Junk Market, & A Fed That Won't Look Through Anything: The Six Biggest Ideas From A Week Of Chaos
key_insights: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia ended July with a $99B equity book (about 13x a year earlier) plus $530.5B of commitments, buy-backs and guarantees in 10-Q footnotes, including a $105B Ohio backstop for OpenAI. The structure is circular: Nvidia buys a stake, the recipient commits to Nvidia hardware, and the cash returns as GPU orders.

UBS's Tim Arcuri estimates NVDA generates about $50-60B per quarter in FCF, much of it recycled into the AI ecosystem. A pause by new management could remove $50B or more from the system, at a time when rates are rising and parts of credit are less liquid.

Goldman's James Schneider expects Nvidia to honor commitments already signed. The next round of commitments is harder. Interim CEO Colette Kress reportedly pushed back on the original OpenAI backstop and cut it in half. Broadcom is backstopping 72.5% of a $63B Anthropic deal versus Nvidia's 25%. Nvidia's valuation is at a 13-year low after a six-week losing streak.

Goldman's head of leveraged finance Miriam Wheeler says non-IG supply has contracted sharply since end-September, with no new deals in the last month, after about 30 AI deals in the prior 12 months. AI-related high yield spreads are about 425bp versus about 265bp for non-AI BB/B paper. A year ago AI junk traded tighter than the rest of the market.

Investment grade tenant wraps on data center deals only become effective on completion. If a developer misses its 180-day grace period, the tenant can walk. Nscale's amended S-1 shows net interest consuming 68 cents of each revenue dollar in the first half, $24B of equipment purchase commitments against $1.48B of cash, and no binding commitments to fund its Anthropic project. CoreWeave guided to a $1.1B quarterly interest bill on $47B of debt. Chip CDS has traded wider than hyperscaler CDS for the first time.

Goldman's 2027 equity outlook (Peter Oppenheimer) sees S&P earnings growth falling from 36% this year to 11% in 2027, with STOXX 600, TOPIX and Asia at least halving. Hyperscaler capex added 12pp to S&P EPS growth this year, fading to 9pp in 2027 as depreciation rises, then a 5pp drag in 2028. Goldman calls hyperscalers, on 19.7x forward earnings and cheaper than Consumer Staples, the defensive growth trade.
The author notes hyperscalers burned $31B of free cash flow in Q3, issued $296B of debt this year against a $250B forecast, and have about $740B more queued for 2027.

Goldman's Jessica Rindels sees US AI spending reaching $1.4T annualized by end-2027, about 4% of GDP, adding only 0.2pp to measured GDP growth. Half the nominal increase is chip price inflation and most hardware is imported. Imported semiconductors for AI make a negative contribution to measured GDP. AI-related debt issuance is $687B this year, 43% from hyperscalers.

Goldman economists (2027 macro outlook, 'Remarkably Unremarkable') say the AI boom has affected earnings and market values more than GDP, and that ongoing financing needs will likely push credit spreads wider. Anthropic is pricing an IPO on Nov 18, reportedly six times covered.

October CPI was hotter than all but one of 70 forecasts and was the third straight hot month. Waller said a 50bp hike 'should be considered' in December. Logan wants at least two more hikes. Goldman added a third hike in March 2027. PPI was up 6.5% y/y, the most since November 2022.

The 2Y yield rose about 35bps on the week, its biggest move since October 2024. The first 10Y auction with a 5% coupon since 2006 saw indirect bidders fall from 80.3% to 61.2%, and all three coupon auctions tailed. Breakevens barely moved, so the move was a real-rate shock. The 10Y is near 5.15%.

The October federal deficit was $404B, the worst October on record, with interest at 28.2% of federal revenue. The dollar broke out of an 18-month range, USDJPY reached 160 and gold fell below $3,900.

BofA's stress index ranks Japan as the most stressed region by a wide margin. The yen funding spread (Tibor-OIS) is the most stressed of its 41 gauges. Japan's FX chief warned of 'excessively rapid' moves.

Goldman's prime book shows US fundamental L/S funds cut gross by 8.7 points in midterm week, the largest drop since March 2020, with net leverage at 43.3%, a five-year low. 55.8M puts traded across US venues the prior week, a record, followed by one of the fastest dumps of protection on record. 1-month realized vol of the VVIX hit 208, above Volmageddon, Covid and Liberation Day.

Vanda recorded the biggest opening bid it has ever seen in NVDA, about 41x normal, on the day Huang resigned. Goldman's Rich Privorotsky says positioning is a tailwind and the Fed is a headwind, and expects chop rather than breakout unless oil and rates fall.

Goldman's Cosimo Codacci-Pisanelli sees a possible early Santa rally on lighter positioning, multiples at 35-year averages and seasonals. World manufactured goods import prices run at about a 24% six-month annualized pace, above the pandemic peak, and January price resets cluster, with about 16 components seeing a 2-sigma reset versus 2.5 or fewer in other months. He calls Q1 the real test.

The author sides with the bond market: a short-covering rally cannot offset a real-rate shock indefinitely. Next catalysts: Kress's first earnings as interim CEO on Tuesday and Anthropic's pricing on Wednesday night. Trump said 'we don't need a deal' with Iran.
